title: Standardize Retry-After & Idempotency Semantics for Streaming + OpenAI-Compat API
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Standardizes 429/503 semantics and Retry-After header handling for streaming endpoints; clarifies idempotency-key behavior for streaming requests; updates OpenAI-compatible layer to surface consistent error codes and headers.
description: Context: multiple production incidents revealed inconsistent Retry-After handling in the OpenAI-compat layer plus unclear idempotency semantics for streaming endpoints (tool/function calls + structured output). Motivation: clients retry logic depends on consistent 429/503 + Retry-After semantics and a clear contract for idempotency keys when partial/streamed responses may have been emitted. This PR unifies server-side semantics across the API stack (hosted runtime, compat adapter, and SDK helpers) and adds tests and docs. Summary of changes: 1) Add canonical Retry-After header middleware that normalizes values from upstreams and ensures RFC-compliant formatting (seconds OR HTTP-date) before reaching the OpenAI-compat adapter. 2) Establish explicit idempotency semantics for streaming endpoints: idempotency-key is accepted for streaming requests, the server will persist a sentinel state when an initial head-chunk is committed to the outgoing stream, and subsequent retries within the configured retention window will return the original accepted operation status (HTTP 409 if conflicting, or the original operation result if available). 3) Update OpenAI-compat adapter to map internal error categories to stable OpenAI-like codes (429 -> rate_limit_exceeded with Retry-After, 503 -> service_unavailable with Retry-After, 500 -> internal_error) and to include the canonical Retry-After header. 4) SDK/compat helpers: expose a helper to parse Retry-After and a small convenience for idempotency-key generation/documentation in the Python SDK. 5) Add integration + unit tests that simulate mid-stream failures and verify retry behavior and idempotency guarantees. Rollout plan: feature flagged on redwood-api (off by default), staged rollout to dedicated customers followed by full enable after 2 days of canary traffic. Checklist: - [x] Add Retry-After middleware and tests - [x] Define idempotency semantics for streaming in docs - [x] Update OpenAI compatibility mapping - [x] SDK helper + docs - [x] Integration tests covering mid-stream retries - [x] Feature flag and rollout notes Testing: unit tests added for header parsing and mapping; integration tests run against local canary runtime with artificial 503 injection; flaky integration test fixed and re-run. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in via feature flag; compat adapter will start surfacing Retry-After when enabled. Follow-ups: measure client-side retry reductions via telemetry (ENG-8270).
